items.title: time for a performance review
items.caption:
my AI chief of staff kept writing replies to emails I had already answered….

(my AI chief of staff is an agent that runs on a schedule; at 6am it runs and creates email drafts in my voice, gathers my to-dos and calendar blocks my schedule before start working)

deleting the incorrect draft took just a second, but soon time started slipping… so it was time for a performance review!

TRY THIS:

THE PERFORMANCE REVIEW;

- pick the ONE output you keep opening and correcting… not every agent you built, one job.
- read the source material and the output side by side, then write down what you had to change. “bad draft” is useless. “this draft promised friday delivery when no date was agreed to” is the actual mistake.
- go back to your original instructions and find what you assumed it knew. mine said “find the emails that need me and draft replies.” obviously that means threads i haven’t answered. obviously. i never wrote it down.

&&&

then the harder question; would you build this same thing again, knowing what you know now?

sometimes no! you’re allowed to change your mind or make the job simper
I would rather have a small job handled well than keep expanding one I don’t trust

the full walkthrough plus the prompts I use are on Le Index; link in bio

items.title: what do you notice that everyone else misses?
items.caption:
some confessions gathered from the AI generation;;;

-AI won’t replace taste: it’ll make having none much more obvious
- the people saying AI is “cheating” are often protecting systems that were already unfair...
-we don’t need AI to make more content; we need it to help us make better decisions
-AI is not the end of creativity... it’s the end of confusing effort with originality
-if your work can be fully replaced by a prompt: maybe the work was never valued properly
-the biggest AI divide won’t be technical skill; it’ll be who knows how to ask better questions
-AI can make everyone more productive... but it cannot decide what is worth producing
-we’re moving from “what can you do?” to “what do you notice that everyone else misses?”
-the future belongs less to people with the best prompts; and more to people with the clearest point of view
-maybe AI isn’t making us less human... maybe it’s forcing us to define what being human at work was supposed to mean
-all of these were made with @chatgpt

items.title: take it one step further
items.caption:
the biggest complaint I get about working with AI is that it gets simple things wrong

the solution??? correct it!

sounds simple, but it’s the only way for AI to improve

an example: this morning @claudeai read through my inbox and drafted responses for me to review this morning
-what AI got wrong: it replied to an old email thread that I had already answered
-how I fixed it: I called it out and said that I had already responded! Claude told me he didn’t finish indexing the thread (oops) and corrected his instructions to fully scroll and analyzing before responding so that it didn’t happen again

take it one step further: ask AI to do it again and make sure the updated instructions are working!

when working with and delegating to AI, not everything will be perfect the first time 
BUT if you take a little extra time and fix mistakes now, you’ll save 10x more time in the future!!!

items.title: Agency is what you actually do about it.
items.caption:
Taste was supposed to be the thing AI couldn’t replace…. then everyone’s taste started looking identical.

Everyone posts the same street, the same book, the same quote and calls it a point of view.

Taste is what you say you’d choose. AGENCY is what you actually do about it.
&&& here’s how I’m using AI with agency:

6AM, EVERY WEEKDAY; MY AI CHIEF OF STAFF
-logs every promise I made in email + Slack as a task in Notion
-drafts replies to the 3 people waiting on me
-blocks 90 minutes for whatever I’m most behind on
-flags anything worth noting in the studio results

6PM, EVERY SUNDAY; MY SALES + REVENUE REPORT
-pulls last week’s numbers, runs them against the week before
-analyzes trends and flags any major changes to our performance
-drafts results in my inbox before I open my laptop

AI does NOT send the emails. I do.
AI does NOT mark anything done. I do.

It CAN tell me one studio performance changed week over week. 
It CANNOT tell me whether that’s the schedule or the trainer, and it cannot decide what I’m willing to change about it.

Taste is what you say you’d choose. Agency is what you actually do about it.

the full essay on why I traded taste for agency is on @substack ;;;
Le Index, link in my bio <3

items.title: teach AI to sound like YOU!!!
items.caption:
I use AI every day, but if I had to start from scratch here are the 3 THINGS I would start doing immediately;;;

1. teach AI to sound like YOU!!!
Your voice, your values, your way of thinking can all be captured in a document. Once it exists, you give it to AI the same way you’d give a new hire context before their first day:

-Ask AI to interview you for a voice profile document for 20 to 100 questions!!! The more questions, the better the profile. I recommend dictating your responses (more on the next slide) to capture your natural responses. 
-Then ask AI to put this into an .md (markdown) file to use with different AI platforms.

—

2. use @wisprflow to dictate rather than type
Wispr  is an AI dictation tool that works everywhere you type, turning natural speech into clean, punctuated text:

-It doesn’t live inside one app the way voice mode lives inside Claude or ChatGPT. You hit a hotkey and you’re dictating straight into Slack, Gmail, Notion, Word, Claude.
-It cleans up filler words on its own and it’s smart enough to know the difference between what you said and what you meant to say.

—

3. if I’ve corrected the same misunderstanding with AI twice, I stop trying to save the chat & START OVER

THEN I PASTE THIS:
Before we continue, audit this entire conversation. Tell me:
1. What was my original goal?
2. What outcome are we currently working toward?
3. What important context, preferences, and constraints have I given you?
4. What decisions have we already made?
5. Which parts of the work are strong and should be preserved?
6. Where have we gone off track, misunderstood each other, or repeated ourselves?
7. What remains unresolved?
8. What information would you need from me to produce the best final result?
Now imagine you are starting this task again with everything you have learned. Write the exact opening prompt I should paste into a new chat to reach my desired outcome faster.
Make the prompt self-contained. Do not refer to this conversation because the new chat will not have access to it.

—

tips like these & more over on @substack !!!

@annanoellerinke
